messages:
maria: quick question — we're seeing tail latency spikes on the fastpath when prefetch kicks in. wants to discuss tradeoffs: prefetching + hedging vs keeping a trimmed fastpath queue.

jon: can you paste a short graph or sample logs? is this correlated with bursty traffic or long sequences?

maria: pasted a tiny sample: `reqs/s` jumps from 120 -> 900 for ~10s, P99 fastpath latency jumps 2x. looks tied to requests that have 2-3x longer KV cache misses.

kevin: my suspicion: prefetch primes KV + model warmup, but it pushes some requests from fastpath into the memory-swap zone. that increases latency variance.

anya: fwiw we've always tuned prefetch heuristics for throughput, not latency. prefetch window size = 8 by default. Shrinking helps latency but hurts token throughput.

maria: tradeoffs we need to weigh: 1) strict fastpath admission (reject prefetch on congested hosts) 2) adaptive prefetch length (shorten when queue grows) 3) hedging to a warm backup model (more cost) 4) fall back to short-circuit responses when trimmed.

jon: +1 for adaptive prefetch. propose: track host-local backlog and reduce prefetch_len = max(1, floor(8 * e^{-backlog/50})). cheap to compute.

kevin: math looks fine but watch for oscillation. if queue drains then expands we might flip-flop. need hysteresis.

anya: also consider admission tagging: add header `x-rw-fastpath-hint: prefer-slim` so upstream can mark low-latency customers. then we can allocate a small reserved slot pool for those.

maria: love the header idea. we'll need policy in gateway: reserved_slots_per_tenant config and a spill policy.

jon: example spill policy: try reserved slot -> fastpath queue -> slowpath (best-effort) -> hedged backup only if slowpath > deadline*0.6.

kevin: on memory/KV impact: when prefetch touches large context (~8k tokens) we pay large KV pressure. maybe add a max_prefetch_bytes threshold per host.

anya: ops implications: tracing will need a `prefetch.trace` span. Also cost accounting: prefetch tokens need to be billed or flagged for internal metrics or customers will be surprised.

maria: good catch. let's add a flag `prefetch_charged: boolean` to decide policy per customer. For trial tiers, maybe not charged to avoid surprise.

ops-bot: deploy-bot posted: rolling deploy of gateway v2.3 started at 2026-03-22T15:12:10Z — monitor p99.

jon: action items: (1) implement adaptive prefetch_len w/ hysteresis (2) header hint + reserved slot plumbing (3) prefetch bytes cap + metric (4) add trace span and billing tag. I'll open an RFC PR with config sketches.

kevin: add simulation before rollout. I'll run microbench with bursty synthetic traffic + cold/warm KV patterns.

anya: I'll draft operator runbook for slot exhaustion and billing disputes.

maria: ok please keep updates in this thread. thanks all :thumbsup:
